exercise.name: Kettlebell Bent Press

reference.title: Kettlebell Bent Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (hip hinge with side bend under a fixed load, then a stand-up with the arm locked)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace in the rack, short breaths behind the brace on the way under, breathe out as you stand up.

prescription.load: User-chosen kettlebell; start light, the bent press allows heavy loads only after long practice
prescription.progression: More reps, then a heavier bell; master the windmill first

cues.text: Feet wider than the hips, both turned about 45 degrees to the left. Kettlebell racked at the right shoulder, elbow on the side of the ribs, forearm vertical; eyes on the bell.
Keep the bell where it is and move the body away: hips out to the right and back, hinge and side-bend to the left, left hand sliding down the left leg, until the right arm is straight.
Arm locked and vertical over the shoulder, chest open toward the bell, right knee straight, left knee soft.
Stand back up with the arm locked, eyes on the bell.
Stand tall with the bell overhead.
Lower the bell back to the rack under control.
Re-set the elbow on the ribs and repeat; switch sides after the set.

mistakes.mistake: Pressing the bell up with the arm
mistakes.fix: The bell stays still; the body moves down and away from it until the arm is straight.
Keep the forearm vertical under the bell the whole way.

mistakes.mistake: Rounding forward instead of hinging and side-bending
mistakes.fix: Push the right hip out and back first; the spine stays long.
Eyes on the bell for the whole rep.

kinematics.norm: Hip hinge with a side bend and an open chest, as in the windmill; no study defines the angles (clinical opinion)
Starts racked with the elbow on the ribs and finishes locked vertical; the bell stays at about the same height while the body moves under it (clinical opinion)
The loaded-side knee straight, the other soft; the hips hinge (clinical opinion)
Slides down the inside of the front leg toward the shin or foot (clinical opinion)
Wider than the hips, turned about 45 degrees away from the kettlebell (clinical opinion)
Slow and controlled, about 2-3 s to get under the bell (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual 17218, Kettlebell Bent Press, video (movement reference)
Konrad, Schmitz and Denner 2001, neuromuscular evaluation of trunk-training exercises (J Athl Train 36(2):109-118; PMC155519)
McGill, Juker and Kropf, quantitative intramuscular myoelectric activity of quadratus lumborum during a wide variety of tasks (Clinical Biomechanics)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp, radiating or nerve-type pain.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
The kettlebell load is user-chosen; learn the windmill and the get-up first and start light.
Shoulder pain, instability or limited overhead mobility: do not hold a weight overhead.
Low-back pain: keep the range small; the hinge and side bend combine under load.
If the bell drifts, let it go to the side and step away; never let it fall over the head.
modify: No weight (bodyweight windmill) or the free hand on a box to shorten the range.
Kettlebell held low in the free hand instead (low windmill).
progressions: Turkish get-up with a heavier bell.

muscleNotes.obliques_r: The obliques on the kettlebell side lower the trunk into the side-bend under control and pull it back up; side-lying lateral flexion work drove external oblique to about 98% MVC in Konrad 2001. No EMG study of the windmill was found (clinical opinion for the windmill itself).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: The obliques on the free-hand side turn the chest open toward the kettlebell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Holds the upper arm out and up as the body moves under the bell (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Steadies the bell in the rack and over the shoulder (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up, the right hip pushed back and out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Both glutes control the hip hinge and drive the stand-up, the right hip pushed back and out (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.spinal_extensors_r: Quadratus lumborum and the erector spinae on the kettlebell side hold the trunk as it hinges and bends; quadratus lumborum is a primary lateral stabiliser (McGill, Juker and Kropf).
muscleNotes.glute_med_r: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Steadies the pelvis over the planted feet as the hips shift (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_r: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the nearly straight right leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.hamstrings_l: Lengthen as the hips hinge over the nearly straight right leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Rectus abdominis and the deep abdominals keep the trunk braced (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.triceps_r: Straightens the elbow as the body bends away; the arm is pushed straight more than it presses (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lats_r: The upper arm rests on the lat in the rack and the lat steadies it as the body turns under (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Keeps the shoulder blade rotated up under the load (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff centres the shoulder as the trunk turns under the fixed arm (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Supports the shoulder girdle under the overhead load (clinical opinion).

guides.label: Bell stays put, the body goes under
Free hand slides down the leg
